notes:
POC focus: enterprise dedicated capacity evaluation for chat + embeddings. Primary ask: throughput guarantees and clear latency SLOs for customer-facing clinical assistant and internal doc-search. Key points from calls/benchmarks: 
- Use-case breakdown: clinical assistant (low latency, streaming preferred), document-search/embeddings (batch/async, throughput-sensitive).
- Latency SLOs: Acme wants p50/p95/p99 defined. They care most about p95 for user experience but legal wants p99 in SLA. Asked for guidance on what we measure vs what they see.
- Measurement alignment discussion notes: 
  * Redwood proposes surface-level SLOs split by metric: "time-to-first-token" (TTFT) and "time-to-last-token" (TTLT) for non-streaming. For streaming, define TTFT + stall-rate (percentage of responses with >1s inter-token gap).
  * Agreement: server-side measurements = ingress timestamp to final-byte-out (Redwood internal). Client-side timing includes network + client decode. Need mapping table in SLA: server SLO -> expected client latency range given region and typical client network (we will provide median network delta by region).
  * Suggested SLO targets (starting point for contract talks): TTFT p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 600ms for typical 2k-context chat on dedicated A100-class pool; TTLT targets expressed as additional delta depending on tokens generated. For streaming, TTFT p50 <= 100-150ms; stall-rate p95 < 2%. (Note: these are baseline guidance; final numbers depend on model, sequence length, and exact GPU SKU).
- Throughput guarantees & reserved GPU planning:
  * Agreed approach: map peak concurrent requests (QPS) * average token output to tokens/sec requirement -> convert to GPUs using Redwood throughput profile per GPU (we provided sample numbers during POC).
  * Acme wants a hard minimum throughput SLA during business hours (09:00-18:00 PT) plus burst buckets off-peak. Discussed overprovisioning buffer (20-30%) for headroom.
  * Action: Priya to deliver a reserved GPU plan spreadsheet (inputs: 99th-percentile tokens/sec per request, expected concurrency, target headroom).
- SLA negotiation items:
  * Measurement definition: define canonical measurement points (ingress, first-byte-out, last-byte-out), sampling granularity, and whether p99 is rolling 30d or 7d. Acme's legal prefers 30d rolling.
  * Remedies: Service credits tied to p99 breaches for time-to-first-token and availability. Acme pushing for higher credits; Redwood offering tiered credits and remediation playbook.
  * Security & compliance addenda: KMS/HSM, audit log retention, residency controls included in Private offering. Need appendix for on-prem deployment differences.
- Benchmark observations & risks:
  * POC runs show consistent p50 but tail increases with long-generation (>4k tokens) flows. Possible mitigations: quantization variants, KV cache warmup, request shaping, and explicit routing to higher-SLA pool.
  * Streaming measurement complexity: client libraries report different timings (time to first token vs time to last token vs decode time). Recommended standard: use server-provided timestamps in response envelope for canonical measurement and expose SDK helper to calculate client delta.
- Next steps (agreed):
  1) Redwood (Priya) to provide reserved-GPU plan (spreadsheet) by 2026-03-05.
  2) Redwood to propose SLO language with measurement definitions and mapping notes (server vs client) in SLA draft by 2026-03-07.
  3) Joint run: 24h stress test targeting peak business-hour mix (Redwood infra + Acme synthetic traffic) week of 2026-03-15.
  4) Legal review: sync 2026-03-10 to go over service credit / p99 windows.
- Quotes/paraphrases: "We need guaranteed tail latency for our clinical flows—patients can't wait. If your p99 slips, we escalate to failover.", procurement: "pricing needs to include reserved GPU ramps and predictable monthly cost; variable overages are OK if capped."
- Stubs/links: pricing deck (/drive/Acme/Redwood/pricing-deck-v3.pdf), SLA draft (/drive/Acme/Redwood/sla-draft-2026-02-25.pdf), fireflies ff_2026-02-05_acme-web-demo.
- Open items for AE/SE: align on final measurement definitions, agree rolling window for p99, finalize reserved GPU counts and burst policy, confirm legal remedy language.
